verdict.rationale: mParticle's Warehouse Sync pulls existing data from Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery and Databricks, with an API, SQL reference and data mapping. Audiences built on that data can then be connected to audience outputs for activation, which is a reverse-ETL-style path that needs no re-instrumented event collection. However, the documented flow ingests (copies) warehouse data into mParticle rather than defining models and audiences in place on warehouse tables. 'Composable Audiences' appears only as a page title with no supporting detail. missing for 10: documented in-warehouse (zero-copy) model and audience definition, detail on Composable Audiences, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can run warehouse-native: define models and audiences on tables already in my warehouse and activate them without re-collecting the data (reverse ETL)

citations.quote: Warehouse Sync ingests data from your own warehouse into mParticle
Once you have created an audience, you must connect it to an audience output where you can activate it.
